key_insight: The paper introduces a smooth, explicit elastoplastic-damage update that preserves loading history with closed-form branches, avoiding local Newton solves for graphics simulation.
engineering_relevance: It offers a compact and vectorizable material model for explicit solvers when smooth activation, irreversibility, and residual deformation are more important than exact yield-surface enforcement.
method: Softplus generates a candidate equivalent plastic strain, then a max-history projection enforces irreversibility.
A deviatoric plastic-strain tensor stores residual direction while an exponential scalar damage variable evolves from the history.
Active and frozen branches are evaluated analytically from one response energy, with no local Newton iteration.
evidence_signal: Across cyclic tension, cantilever bending, platen compression, and a torus test, the method reproduces residual deformation and monotone internal variables, while the baseline J2 radial-return kernel is faster by 1.51–3.08×.
watch_item: The approach is intended for isotropic, proportional or nearly proportional loading; large path-direction changes can produce substantial error.
paper_title: A Smooth Explicit Elastoplastic--Damage Update for Graphics Simulation
